title: Tôi cần bác sĩ
summary: Say "I need a doctor" with Tôi cần bác sĩ, then use the notes below to adjust tone and next steps.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: For travelers, Tôi cần bác sĩ is the phrase to keep ready for "I need a doctor" in doctors, pharmacies, symptoms, and medication. This helps if you feel sick and need medical help quickly. It works best when you focus on putting the need first and leaving room for the helper to confirm the detail. After you say it, listen for a confirmation, a handoff, a price, or a follow-up question; the next rows help you keep the exchange moving.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: Listen to each piece, then the whole phrase, so the rhythm feels connected instead of memorized word by word.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Use Tôi cần bác sĩ as your first sentence for "I need a doctor". This helps if you feel sick and need medical help quickly. Leave a short pause after the phrase so the other person can answer with a confirmation, a handoff, a price, or a follow-up question. Keep the affected area, passport copy, location, or helper contact visible if it helps the other person act.

sections.title: Why it matters
sections.body: Health phrases need to be simple because the other person may need to act quickly or ask a follow-up. For "I need a doctor", Tôi cần bác sĩ helps by putting the need first and leaving room for the helper to confirm the detail. Pause after the phrase so the person can confirm before you add more words.

sections.title: Traveler insight
sections.body: In Health & Pharmacy, the reply often comes as a confirmation, a handoff, a price, or a follow-up question. Say Tôi cần bác sĩ once, pause, and watch for the reply before adding another sentence. Keep the affected area, passport copy, location, or helper contact visible if it helps the other person act.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Keep urgent medical needs clear and direct. A short sentence gives helpers something they can act on quickly.
